summary:
Keep a stack of runs: (tile, how many in a row). A new tile either extends the top run or starts a new one; when
a run reaches k it's crushed by popping it, which automatically lets the run below meet the next tiles. One
pass, O(n), and the result is the stack's runs written out.

question.md:
Repeatedly crush any k identical adjacent tiles until none remain. Return the final row.

- **Chain reactions:** crushing `bbb` in `abbba` (k = 3) brings the two `a`s together, and with a third `a` they
  could crush too.
- **The order of crushes doesn't change the result** (given in the statement), so any convenient order works.
- **Size:** up to 10⁵ tiles; repeatedly rescanning after each crush is too slow.

think.md:
Take `abbbacca` with k = 3. Crush `bbb`: `aacca`. No other run of 3 yet... `cc` isn't long enough, so the result is
`aacca`.

A crush affects only what's immediately to its left and right. Process tiles left to right while remembering the
runs to the left: when a run is completed and removed, the run before it becomes the new neighbour of the next
tile. "The most recent unfinished run" is the top of a stack; storing counts with each run makes the k-check
O(1).

approaches.title: Find and crush, repeat

idea.md: Scan for any k identical adjacent tiles; remove them; rescan from the start. Stop when a full scan finds nothing.

build: Loop: scan, keeping the length of the current run of equal tiles.
When it reaches k, cut those tiles out and restart.
Stop when a scan completes with no cut.

lines.text: Keep going while the last scan crushed something.
Length of the current run of equal tiles.
A run of k: remove it and rescan from the beginning (neighbours may now form new runs).

complexity.md: **Time O(n² / k)** scans of O(n) each in the worst case (each crush removes k tiles). **Space O(n).**

walk.title: Find any run of 3 identical tiles, remove it, and start over; stop when no run is left.

limits.md: Every crush triggers a full rescan, although only the tiles around the crush can change. A stack keeps exactly that neighbourhood at hand.

approaches.title: Stack of (tile, run length)

idea.md: For each tile: if it equals the top run's tile, increment that run's count, popping it when the count hits k; otherwise push (tile, 1). Finally, write each remaining run out.

build: Extend or push; pop at count k.
Concatenate `tile × count` for the remaining runs.

lines.text: Runs still standing, left to right, each with its length.

lines.text: Same tile as the top run: it grows.
A run reaching k disappears; the run beneath becomes the top and can be extended by the next tiles.
A different tile starts a new run.
Write the surviving runs out in order.

complexity.md: **Time O(n):** each tile is pushed or counted once, and popped at most once. **Space O(n).**

steps.text: 'b' makes a run of 3: crush it (pop).

walk.title: Stack of (tile, run length). A tile equal to the top extends its run; reaching k pops it. Otherwise push a new run of 1.

takeaways.md:
- "Remove adjacent groups, then let neighbours meet" → stack, so the new neighbour is always the top.
- Store **(value, count)** on the stack to check run lengths in O(1).
